result_text:
All four broken default conventions now match their intended files. The new test class and the existing `SourceFileFilterTest` pass offline (`mvn -o -pl codeanalyzer test`). Nothing is committed.

**Changes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:**
- **Generated HTML (pkgdown, Doxygen, meta generator):** the extension group `(html|html|xhtml)` is now `(htm|html|xhtml)`, so `.htm` pages are covered.
- **.NET doc XML:** the path pattern `.*/[.]xml` is now `.*[.]xml`, so `MyAssembly.xml` matches.
- **Generated JavaScript (`// Generated by …`):** the path pattern `.*/[.]js` is now `.*[.]js`, so `app.js` matches.
- **Gradle JavaScript scripts:** the path pattern `.*/[.][-]gradle[.]js` is now `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches.

**New test:** `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It checks that the four fixed rules match the intended files and that the older cases still match (Doxygen `.html`, `.xhtml` with a generator meta tag, `build.gradle`). It also checks that hand-written `.htm`, `.html`, `.js` and `.xml` files stay out of the generated scope.

One thing I noticed but did not change: the content-only rule `//[ ]*Generated by .*` has no path pattern and no line limit, so any `.js` file containing a line like `// Generated by …` anywhere is classed as generated, whatever its name. That is outside the four fixes you asked for. My first negative JS fixture hit it, so I changed the fixture's wording instead.
